answers.rationale: Pool-a at 60 s had baseline duplicates on Sep 17 and, after Sep 18, baseline duplicates for jobs of 500 or fewer recipients.
Pool-b and us-east see the same 95 s p99 durations for large jobs but baseline duplicate rates.
Only pool-a (60 s) large jobs after Sep 18 (p99 95 s) show elevated duplicates; the queue makes a job re-visible if not deleted within the timeout and the provider does not de-duplicate.
The marketing/transactional split is confounded with recipient count; marketing jobs in pool-b and us-east and small marketing jobs in pool-a show baseline rates.
Worker counts differ across pools, but no analysis relates them to pick-up of re-visible jobs.
Only the p99 (95 s) is reported; the share of calls above 120 s is not known, so 'all' cannot be established or ruled out.
The timeout produces duplicates only for jobs whose calls outlast 60 s, which occur only for large jobs after Sep 18.
The provider change raises duplicates only where the timeout is 60 s.
eu-west pool-b at 300 s has baseline rates with the same job mix; the regional difference is the timeout configuration.
Holding recipient count and pool fixed, marketing jobs show baseline rates.
Small-job p99 is 12 s before and after.
eu-west pool-b shares the network and shows baseline rates; pool-a small jobs are also at baseline.
Durations are the same in all pools regardless of timeout.
Large jobs are duplicated only in pool-a after Sep 18; neither before the provider change nor in 300 s pools.
Removes one of the jointly required conditions; 300 s pools show baseline rates with the same durations.
Removes the other jointly required condition; small calls take 12 s p99 and the rate limit has ample headroom.
Acts on the apparent regional main effect and would process EU personal data outside eu-west, violating the data-handling policy.
Rests on the provider change being sufficient alone; us-east and pool-b marketing sends are unaffected.
Sep 17 safety held only because calls were short; with current 95 s p99 for large jobs, a 60 s timeout would reproduce the duplicates in pool-b and us-east.
Template engine v2 runs in all pools, which show baseline rates outside the joint condition.
